![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Passing `normalizeString` directly to `Array.prototype.map` causes its second parameter (`fallback`) to be bound to the array element's `index`. When an element is empty or falsy, `normalizeString` falls back to the index value (e.g., `1`, `2`, etc.), which is truthy and gets preserved by `.filter(Boolean)`. This injects unexpected indices into the unique strings array. Use an explicit arrow function to ensure only the first argument is passed.

```suggestion
function uniqueStrings(values) {
  return [...new Set(values.map((val) => normalizeString(val)).filter(Boolean))];
}
```

The condition `visualRequired === false` in `studentQuestionDisplay` prevents any visual-required question from ever being displayed to the student, even when `blocked` is `false` (meaning all visual gates have passed). This directly contradicts `studentFacingQuestionAttemptable` in `buildAttemptability`, which is `true` when `blocked` is `false` and availability is `'attemptable'`. Remove the `visualRequired === false` restriction so that unblocked visual-required questions can be displayed.

```javascript
    studentQuestionDisplay: !blocked && normalizeToken(posture.questionAvailability) === 'attemptable',
```
